Definition: from G18; goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence:--goodness.
BiblicalUsage: Agathosyne is goodness — virtue, beneficence, the quality of being good and doing good. Paul says the Romans are 'full of goodness,' names goodness as fruit of the Spirit, says the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth, and prays that God would fulfil every good pleasure of His goodness in the Thessalonians. The word is always active: goodness that fills, bears fruit, and overflows.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this word is the difference between being good and doing good. Goodness as the Spirit grows it does not sit still — it fills a church, it bears fruit, it fulfils God's good pleasure — and that is the goodness I want to be full of.
